correctness.rationale: Even n=2m height sliding windows at time m-2 have length m-1. For mass n-1, an increase after shifting by two is equivalent to a unique exceptional peak h_k>=h_(k+2j)+2 for all 1<=j<m. Drift -1 excludes a second peak. After fixing its location, increments force a -1,-1 start and two endpoint alternatives; remaining paired paths have transfer K=T^2+e0e0^T. The formal rank-one resolvent and odd/even parts of the Motzkin quadratic identity prove rooted count 2M_(n-3) and total count 2nM_(n-3). Complementation gives mass n+1. A local central limit calculation yields conditional probability 2/9. All finite checks pass but are not the infinite proof.

value.rationale: The nearest off-critical occupied masses n±1 are a natural, physically significant sector for slow deterministic capacity-two traffic relaxation. For every even circumference the exact last-entry population equals 2nM_(n-3), and a surprising positive 2/9 proportion of that exact-mass sector remains maximally delayed. A genuinely nontrivial parity-sampled Motzkin boundary correction is needed, not merely evaluating a pre-existing recurrent-language transfer. The incomplete exactly critical census does not undermine the natural complete adjacent-density result.
